, not permanent loss in most cases, but the interim created incorrect throttling behavior and billing preview mismatches. hypothesis : during migration we rely on a dual - write handoff with an optimistic cutover. if the streaming delta pipeline has backpressure or message reorder combined with non - idempotent debit operations, we can drop increments or double - apply depending on race conditions. specifically : ( a ) old - shard may stop decrementing allowance before new - shard has replayed all in - flight events, creating a transient invisible - consumption window ; ( b ) the reconciliation job is eventually consistent, so counts reconcile late. race with per - route quota enforcement and the token - bucket refill scheduler produces transient incorrect throttle decisions.

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/slack",
    "content": "{\n  \"content\": \"alex_support: Customer reports Python SDK streaming generator hangs when the first SSE chunk contains a partial token. They say streaming output stops and generator never yields final text.\\n\\nnina_support: Can you paste the SDK version + minimal repro? Also any raw logs from the app (showing bytes) would help.\\n\\nalex_support: Customer env: python 3.10, httpx 0.24.3, redwood-python 0.6.1. Repro steps they gave:\\n1) open stream with client.stream(...) using default SDK helper\\n2) iterate generator\\n3) sometimes it yields nothing (hangs) until connection closes\\n\\nben_eng: Likely SSE parsing edge-case where the first network chunk ends mid-json token (e.g. \\\"{\\\\\\\"delta\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Hel\\\") and parser waits for the event terminator `\\\\n\\\\n`. Need a tiny reproducer.\\n\\nalex_support: Here's their raw bytes capture (redacted):\\n```\\n--- chunk 1 ---\\ndata: {\\\"id\\\":\\\"evt_1\\\",\\\"delta\\\":\\\"Hel\\n--- chunk 2 ---\\nlo\\\",\\\"role\\\":\\\"assistant\\\"}\\n\\n--- chunk 3 ---\\ndata: {\\\"id\\\":\\\"evt_2\\\",\\\"delta\\\":\\\" worl\\\"\\n```\\nIn that trace, the generator paused after chunk 1 and didn't flush the partial JSON when chunk 2 arrived.\\n\\ntim_pysdk: That matches bug we fixed last week \\u2014 parser didn't handle partial JSON boundaries correctly when the first event lacked a trailing empty line or when keepalive frames (204/empty `data:`) are interleaved. Fixed in redwood-python 0.6.2. Workaround: use the lower-level `.stream_raw()` and accumulate bytes yourself or upgrade.\\n\\ntori_sre: Additional note: some HTTP client versions (httpx/urllib3) split TCP frames differently which makes this flaky. Repro is sensitive to `httpx` version + OS socket buffer. If you can't upgrade, we can add a small shim to the SDK to flush incomplete events after a short idle (100ms) \\u2014 less ideal but pragmatic.\\n\\nalex_support: Minimal repro script customer ran (sanitized):\\n```\\nfrom redwood import RedwoodClient\\nc = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)\\nit = c.stream(\\\"chat:generate\\\", model=\\\"redwood/latest\\\")\\nfor chunk in it:\\n    print(repr(chunk))\\n```\\nThey also provided a custom raw loop that shows the SSE frame split.\\n\\nnina_support: Can you ask customer to try `pip install redwood-python==0.6.2` and confirm? If they can't, collect a tcpdump or `curl --raw` trace.\\n\\nci-bot: Deploy note: redwood-python 0.6.2 released to PyPI (chore/stream-sse-fix). See changelog: https://pypi.org/project/redwood-python/0.6.2\\n\\nben_eng: For triage: if they reproduce locally, collect these items: 1) Python version, 2) httpx version, 3) minimal script + exact output, 4) raw bytes capture from `scapy`/tcpdump or middleware, 5) SDK logs with DEBUG.\\n\\ntim_pysdk: Internals: parser now accumulates until a full event delimiter or EOF, and will also try to parse partial JSON when a `data:` line ends with an incomplete brace and the next chunk arrives. This avoids generator deadlock on split tokens.\\n\\nnina_support: Customer upgraded and reported back: \\\"issue seems fixed \\u2014 streaming resumed immediately and tokens arrive as expected\\\" :thumbsup:\\n\\nalex_support: Closing with notes for the ticket: root cause = SSE parser did not handle JSON split across chunk boundary + httpx chunking. Fix in 0.6.2. Repro steps and raw bytes attached to ticket. Marked resolved.\\n\\nben_eng: Follow-up: add unit test that simulates chunking at random offsets and a stress test in CI (httpx compatibility matrix), open follow-up GH issue to test against older httpx versions.\\n\\ntori_sre: Also add a short troubleshooting FAQ blurb for support: \\\"If streaming hangs, ask customer to upgrade SDK and report http client version + raw bytes\\\".\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"content\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_bd52d657b63a4a4ba589e05e78182d9f\"\n}",

{
  "content": "alex_support: Customer reports Python SDK streaming generator hangs when the first SSE chunk contains a partial token. They say streaming output stops and generator never yields final text.

nina_support: Can you paste the SDK version + minimal repro? Also any raw logs from the app (showing bytes) would help.

alex_support: Customer env: python 3.10, httpx 0.24.3, redwood-python 0.6.1. Repro steps they gave:
1) open stream with client.stream(...) using default SDK helper
2) iterate generator
3) sometimes it yields nothing (hangs) until connection closes

ben_eng: Likely SSE parsing edge-case where the first network chunk ends mid-json token (e.g. "{\"delta\":\"Hel") and parser waits for the event terminator `\n\n`. Need a tiny reproducer.

alex_support: Here's their raw bytes capture (redacted):
```
--- chunk 1 ---
data: {"id":"evt_1","delta":"Hel
--- chunk 2 ---
lo","role":"assistant"}

--- chunk 3 ---
data: {"id":"evt_2","delta":" worl"
```
In that trace, the generator paused after chunk 1 and didn't flush the partial JSON when chunk 2 arrived.

tim_pysdk: That matches bug we fixed last week — parser didn't handle partial JSON boundaries correctly when the first event lacked a trailing empty line or when keepalive frames (204/empty `data:`) are interleaved. Fixed in redwood-python 0.6.2. Workaround: use the lower-level `.stream_raw()` and accumulate bytes yourself or upgrade.

tori_sre: Additional note: some HTTP client versions (httpx/urllib3) split TCP frames differently which makes this flaky. Repro is sensitive to `httpx` version + OS socket buffer. If you can't upgrade, we can add a small shim to the SDK to flush incomplete events after a short idle (100ms) — less ideal but pragmatic.

alex_support: Minimal repro script customer ran (sanitized):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
it = c.stream("chat:generate", model="redwood/latest")
for chunk in it:
    print(repr(chunk))
```
They also provided a custom raw loop that shows the SSE frame split.

nina_support: Can you ask customer to try `pip install redwood-python==0.6.2` and confirm? If they can't, collect a tcpdump or `curl --raw` trace.

ci-bot: Deploy note: redwood-python 0.6.2 released to PyPI (chore/stream-sse-fix). See changelog: https://pypi.org/project/redwood-python/0.6.2

ben_eng: For triage: if they reproduce locally, collect these items: 1) Python version, 2) httpx version, 3) minimal script + exact output, 4) raw bytes capture from `scapy`/tcpdump or middleware, 5) SDK logs with DEBUG.

tim_pysdk: Internals: parser now accumulates until a full event delimiter or EOF, and will also try to parse partial JSON when a `data:` line ends with an incomplete brace and the next chunk arrives. This avoids generator deadlock on split tokens.

nina_support: Customer upgraded and reported back: "issue seems fixed — streaming resumed immediately and tokens arrive as expected" :thumbsup:

alex_support: Closing with notes for the ticket: root cause = SSE parser did not handle JSON split across chunk boundary + httpx chunking. Fix in 0.6.2. Repro steps and raw bytes attached to ticket. Marked resolved.

ben_eng: Follow-up: add unit test that simulates chunking at random offsets and a stress test in CI (httpx compatibility matrix), open follow-up GH issue to test against older httpx versions.

tori_sre: Also add a short troubleshooting FAQ blurb for support: "If streaming hangs, ask customer to upgrade SDK and report http client version + raw bytes".
",

    "content"

    "content": "{
  "title": "SDK Parity Matrix: Auth, Retries, Timeouts, Streaming, and Error Taxonomy (Python / TypeScript / Go)",
  "space": "eng-developer-experience",
  "author": "Ibrahim Khan",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "in_review",
  "created_at": "2026-01-18",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-21",
  "reviewers": [
    "Monica Patel",
    "Dana Lo",

    "Marcus Lin",

  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/sdk-parity-audit-overview.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json",
    "sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sdk-auth-resolution-and-secret-handling.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-retry-policy-v1.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-timeout-model.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "## Purpose\nThis page is the working parity matrix for the cross-language SDK parity initiative. It documents **current behavior** and **target behavior** across:\n- **redwood-sdk-python**\n- **redwood-sdk-typescript**\n- **redwood-sdk-go**\n\nThe matrix is used as:\n1) the source-of-truth for what \u201cparity\u201d means for auth/retry/timeout/streaming/error behavior,\n2) the checklist for code changes and docs updates, and\n3) the basis for the cross-language conformance test suite.\n\n## Scope\nIn scope:\n- API key / bearer token auth resolution order, env var naming, headers\n- Retry policy: retryable status codes, network errors, backoff/jitter, respect Retry-After\n- Timeout model: connect/read/overall semantics and defaults\n- Streaming behavior: disconnects, partial output, cancellation, retry guidance\n- Error taxonomy: typed errors + standardized fields (request_id, retry_count, timeout_ms, etc.)\n\nOut of scope:\n- New auth mechanisms (e.g., OAuth flows)\n- Major API surface redesign\n- Streaming \u201cexactly once\u201d semantics (SDKs remain conservative; idempotency guidance is documented)\n\n## Target Standard (summary)\nThis is the parity target (see linked standards/ADRs for the full rationale):\n\n### Auth resolution order (all SDKs)\n1. **Explicit client configuration** (e.g., constructor `api_key` / `token`)\n2. **Environment variables** (preferred names)\n3. Optional: shared config file is **not** supported in v1 parity scope\n\nPreferred env vars:\n- `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (primary)\n- `REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN` (if using bearer tokens)\n- `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` (optional; defaults to hosted API)\n\nHeader rules:\n- API key: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (consistent across SDKs)\n- Never log secrets; error messages must be redaction-safe\n\n### Retry policy defaults (all SDKs)\n- Max attempts: **4 total** (1 initial + up to 3 retries)\n- Retryable HTTP status codes:\n  - **429** (rate limited) \u2014 must respect `Retry-After`\n  - **408** (request timeout)\n  - **409** (conflict) only when `code` indicates transient (see error taxonomy below)\n  - **5xx** (500, 502, 503, 504)\n- Retryable network errors:\n  - DNS errors, connection refused/reset, TLS handshake errors, socket timeouts, unexpected EOF\n- Non-retryable:\n  - **4xx** by default (400, 401, 403, 404, 422) unless explicitly documented and flagged retryable by server error `code`\n- Backoff:\n  - Exponential backoff with jitter\n  - Base delay: **250ms**\n  - Max delay: **8s**\n  - Jitter: full jitter (random in [0, delay])\n- Retry-After:\n  - Parse `Retry-After` as either seconds or HTTP date\n  - When present and valid, it overrides backoff for the next sleep (bounded by a max of 60s)\n\n### Timeout model defaults (all SDKs)\nTimeouts are expressed as **overall** plus optional granular timeouts.\n- Default connect timeout: **10s**\n- Default read timeout (non-streaming): **60s**\n- Default overall timeout (non-streaming): **90s**\n- Streaming:\n  - Overall timeout applies to request setup (connect + first byte)\n  - Streaming read is governed by an **idle timeout** (no bytes received) default **30s** (configurable)\n  - Streaming must support user cancellation (AbortController/context/cancel token) and must terminate promptly\n\n### Streaming retry guidance (all SDKs)\n- **No automatic retry after partial streaming output** (to avoid duplicate side effects / duplicated tokens)\n- If the connection fails **before first content event**, SDK may retry (subject to retry policy) when safe\n- If failure happens **after partial output**, SDK raises a typed streaming interruption error containing:\n  - request_id (if known)\n  - bytes/events received count (best effort)\n  - partial text (if buffering is enabled) or the last event seen\n- Docs recommend:\n  - use request_id for support\n  - use idempotency keys for non-streaming or \u201csafe-to-retry\u201d flows\n\n### Error taxonomy + fields (all SDKs)\nAll SDKs should expose typed errors with consistent fields:\n- `message` (string; redaction-safe)\n- `request_id` (string; from response headers/body when available)\n- `status_code` (int; if HTTP response exists)\n- `code` (string; Redwood error code enum)\n- `retryable` (bool)\n- `retry_after_ms` (int; when available)\n- `attempt` / `retries` (int; how many retries already performed)\n- `timeout_ms` (int; the configured timeout that triggered the failure, when applicable)\n- `cause` / `wrapped_error` (language-native error, if exposed)\n\n\n---\n\n## Parity Matrix\nLegend:\n- \u2705 = matches target\n- \u26a0\ufe0f = partially matches / edge cases\n- \u274c = mismatch\n\n### A) Authentication\n| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Env var names recognized | \u26a0\ufe0f `REDWOOD_API_KEY` plus legacy `RW_API_KEY` in some examples | \u26a0\ufe0f `REDWOOD_API_KEY` + `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in older versions | \u26a0\ufe0f `REDWOOD_API_KEY` + `REDWOOD_BEARER` in older builds | `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN`, `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` only (legacy allowed with deprecation warnings) | Align naming; add migration messaging | Sabrina / Dana / Mateusz |\n| Resolution order | \u26a0\ufe0f explicit param wins; env fallback; but error text differs by path | \u2705 explicit param wins; env fallback | \u26a0\ufe0f env sometimes overrides when both set due to init helper | Explicit > env > error | Fix Go init helper precedence; standardize error text | Mateusz |\n| Header format | \u2705 `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | \u26a0\ufe0f some endpoints set `X-Api-Key` in older compatibility layer | \u2705 Bearer | Bearer everywhere | TS must stop emitting `X-Api-Key` unless explicitly configured (compat) | Dana |\n| Missing auth error | \u26a0\ufe0f raises generic ValueError with setup message | \u26a0\ufe0f throws Error without remediation guidance | \u26a0\ufe0f returns error without indicating env var names | Typed AuthError with message listing supported env vars (no secret echo) | Standardize message template | Ibrahim |\n| Secret redaction in logs | \u26a0\ufe0f redacts in most paths, but debug mode can leak headers in Python | \u2705 redacts | \u26a0\ufe0f Go debug logs included full headers in one helper | Never log `Authorization`; redact known token patterns | Security signoff required; add tests | Marcus + language owners |\n\n\n### B) Retry Policy / Backoff / Retry-After\n| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Default max attempts | \u26a0\ufe0f 3 total in some clients; 4 in others | \u2705 4 total | \u26a0\ufe0f 5 total (historical) | 4 total | Align defaults + docs | Ibrahim |\n| Retryable status codes | \u26a0\ufe0f retries 429 + 5xx; 408 inconsistent | \u26a0\ufe0f one bug: retried 400 in middleware edge case | \u26a0\ufe0f retries 429 + 5xx but missed 408 | Retry 429/408/5xx; 409 only when transient | Fix TS 400 retry; include 408 across all | Dana / Sabrina / Mateusz |\n| Network error retries | \u2705 connection errors retried | \u26a0\ufe0f fetch abort handling categorized incorrectly | \u2705 net/http errors retried | Retry network errors; do not retry user cancellations | TS must differentiate AbortController cancel vs network failure | Dana |\n| Backoff + jitter | \u26a0\ufe0f exponential but jitter differs; base delay not consistent | \u26a0\ufe0f jitter added but not full-jitter | \u2705 close to target | Base 250ms; max 8s; full jitter | Normalize algorithms; align test fixtures | Ibrahim |\n| Retry-After parsing | \u2705 parses seconds; date format missing | \u2705 parses seconds + date | \u274c ignores Retry-After | Parse seconds/date; override backoff; max 60s | Go must implement; Python add date parsing | Mateusz / Sabrina |\n| Retry instrumentation fields | \u26a0\ufe0f logs attempt count but not standardized keys | \u26a0\ufe0f request_id missing on some retry errors | \u274c no consistent fields | Standard fields: request_id, retry_count, retry_reason, retry_after_ms | Align logging schema; docs | Logan Wright + Nadia Rahman |\n\n\n### C) Timeouts\n| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Timeout configuration surface | \u26a0\ufe0f `timeout` overloaded; connect/read not consistently exposed | \u26a0\ufe0f per-request abort only; defaults not obvious | \u2705 context + client timeout exists, but mapping inconsistent | Provide overall + connect/read/idle (stream) where supported; map consistently | Align naming + docs snippets across languages | Ibrahim + language owners |\n| Default connect timeout | \u26a0\ufe0f 5s in one client | \u2705 10s | \u26a0\ufe0f OS default (unbounded) when context missing | 10s | Ensure Go always sets connect timeout when using default client | Mateusz |\n| Default overall timeout (non-stream) | \u26a0\ufe0f 60s | \u2705 90s | \u26a0\ufe0f 120s | 90s | Normalize; include migration notes | Henry + DevEx |\n| Streaming timeout semantics | \u274c streaming ignored `timeout` in iterator path (support driver SUP-29410) | \u26a0\ufe0f abort cancels fetch, but idle timeout not implemented | \u26a0\ufe0f context cancel works, but idle timeout not consistent | Streaming: connect/first-byte uses overall; read idle timeout default 30s | Implement idle timeout for TS/Go; fix Python honoring timeouts in stream | Sabrina / Dana / Mateusz |\n| User cancellation | \u2705 `KeyboardInterrupt`/cancel bubbles; explicit cancel supported | \u2705 AbortController supported | \u2705 context cancellation supported | All must stop promptly and surface as CancelledError (not retryable) | Ensure cancellation is never retried; consistent error type | Ibrahim |\n\n\n### D) Streaming Semantics / Edge Cases\n| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Event model | \u26a0\ufe0f yields raw chunks in some examples; structured events elsewhere | \u2705 structured events (`message.delta`, `message.completed`, etc.) | \u26a0\ufe0f mixed: some helpers emit raw lines | Standardize event names + payload fields in docs; keep language-idiomatic wrappers | Docs + examples must match; conformance fixtures for event ordering | Wei Chen + language owners |\n| Partial output on disconnect | \u26a0\ufe0f partial text lost if exception thrown mid-chunk | \u2705 surfaces partial text in most cases | \u26a0\ufe0f surfaces last event only | Typed StreamingInterruptedError includes partial output when available | Decide buffering policy (memory tradeoff) and document it | Ibrahim + Henry |\n| Disconnect classification | \u26a0\ufe0f raised as generic connection error | \u26a0\ufe0f sometimes treated as retryable network error even after content | \u26a0\ufe0f ambiguous EOF vs server close | If disconnect after content: not auto-retry; raise streaming interruption (retryable=false) | Fix classification and retry suppression | Dana / Mateusz |\n| Retry behavior for streaming | \u26a0\ufe0f may retry pre-first-event; inconsistent | \u26a0\ufe0f retried after some events in one path | \u2705 generally no retry after events | Only retry if no content delivered yet; never after partial | Conformance test should simulate \u201cfirst token then FIN\u201d | Ibrahim |\n| Proxy buffering / keep-alives | \u26a0\ufe0f no documented guidance | \u26a0\ufe0f no documented guidance | \u26a0\ufe0f some guidance in README only | Document recommended keep-alive/idle timeout settings and proxy caveats | Capture in streaming guide + quickstarts | Wei Chen |\n\n\n### E) Error Taxonomy (Typed Errors + Fields)\n| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Base error type | \u26a0\ufe0f multiple base classes across modules | \u26a0\ufe0f Error subclasses exist but missing consistent fields | \u26a0\ufe0f errors wrap net/http without stable fields | Single family: RedwoodError + typed subclasses | Align naming; publish mapping table | Ibrahim |\n| request_id propagation | \u26a0\ufe0f missing on some streaming exceptions | \u2705 present for most HTTP errors | \u274c missing in some cases | request_id always present when server emitted it; best effort on network failures | Requires gateway + SDK work; ensure header parsing in all clients | Ethan Park + language owners |\n| retryable flag | \u26a0\ufe0f computed ad-hoc | \u26a0\ufe0f present but not always accurate | \u274c absent | Always compute using standard classifier; included on error | Shared classifier behavior via fixtures | Ibrahim |\n| Error `code` field | \u26a0\ufe0f present only when JSON body parses | \u2705 present | \u26a0\ufe0f present but naming differs | Use Redwood error code enum; consistent string values | Ensure OpenAI-compat surfaces same fields | Ibrahim |\n| Safe error messages (no secrets) | \u26a0\ufe0f some include base URL with query params | \u2705 safe | \u2705 safe | No tokens/headers; sanitize URLs; include remediation | Add lint/tests for common secret patterns | Marcus Lin |\n\n\n---\n\n## Open Questions / Decisions Needed\n1) **Legacy env vars support window**: Do we allow `RW_API_KEY` / `REDWOOD_TOKEN` / `REDWOOD_BEARER` for one minor release with deprecation warnings, or do we drop immediately?\n   - Proposed: support for **2 minor releases**, with warnings and migration guide.\n\n2) **Streaming buffering policy** for partial output: Should SDKs buffer full generated text by default to include it in StreamingInterruptedError?\n   - Proposed: default **no full buffering** (stream-first), but include:\n     - `last_event` (always)\n     - optional `partial_text` when the SDK already has it (e.g., user concatenates deltas)\n     - optional `buffer_output=true` option (document memory risk)\n\n3) **409 retry semantics**: Which error codes should be considered transient (retryable) under 409?\n   - Proposed: retry 409 only when server error `code` in allowlist (to be defined in error code enum docs).\n\n4) **Timeout defaults for enterprise**: Some customers want stricter defaults (e.g., overall 30s). Do we provide a named preset (e.g., `timeouts=\"interactive\"`) or keep only numeric config?\n   - Proposed: numeric config only for v1 parity; presets can be introduced later.\n\n5) **Telemetry/analytics**: For environments where telemetry is not permitted, do we require standardized structured logs only?\n   - Proposed: minimum requirement is standardized logger/hook fields; telemetry remains opt-in per SDK policy.\n\n\n## Acceptance Criteria (Parity Definition)\nParity is \u201cdone\u201d when all conditions below are met:\n\n### Functional parity\n- Auth:\n  - Explicit credentials always override env vars\n  - Env var names and missing-auth errors are consistent (including remediation text)\n  - Secrets are never logged in any mode\n- Retries:\n  - Same retryable status codes and network errors\n  - Same defaults: max_attempts=4, base=250ms, max=8s, full jitter\n  - All SDKs respect Retry-After (seconds + HTTP date)\n  - Cancellation is never retried\n- Timeouts:\n  - Defaults match (connect=10s, read=60s, overall=90s)\n  - Streaming honors connect/first-byte timeouts and idle timeout (30s default)\n- Streaming:\n  - No automatic retries after partial output\n  - Typed streaming interruption errors contain request_id when available and a stable reason\n- Errors:\n  - Typed errors across SDKs expose: message, request_id, status_code, code, retryable, retry_after_ms, attempt/retries\n\n### Test and docs parity\n- Conformance suite passes for all SDKs:\n  - 429 + Retry-After seconds\n  - 429 + Retry-After HTTP date\n  - 5xx retry with jitter bounds\n  - network reset mid-request\n  - streaming disconnect before first event (may retry)\n  - streaming disconnect after N events (must not auto-retry)\n- Docs pages and quickstarts show the same option names and recommended defaults across languages.\n\n### Operational readiness\n- Standardized log/hook fields available:\n  - `request_id`, `retry_count`, `retry_reason`, `retry_after_ms`, `timeout_ms`, `streaming_disconnect_reason`\n- Rollout dashboard includes dimensions by SDK + version (where available).\n\n\n## Notes on Top Support Drivers (why we\u2019re doing this)\n- Streaming timeouts not honored in Python streaming iterator path (repro\u2019d; aligns with SUP-29410)\n- TS retry bug retried non-retryable 400 in one middleware edge case (billing concern; SUP-29438)\n- Go ignored Retry-After on 429 (burst retries; SUP-29477)\n- Enterprise proxy environments cause streaming disconnects; need consistent error surfaces + guidance (SUP-29505)\n\n\n## Change Tracking / How to Update This Matrix\n- Each row should be updated when:\n  - a parity PR merges, or\n  - conformance tests uncover a mismatch\n- When updating, include:\n  - \u201ccurrent\u201d column changes (what is now true)\n  - \u201cgap/notes\u201d updates (what remains)\n  - link to the PR/ticket in the appropriate repo (via the parity epic)\n\n## Ownership\n- DRI: Monica Patel\n- Tech lead: Ibrahim Khan\n- Language owners: Dana Lo (TS), Mateusz Zielinski (Go), Sabrina James (Python)\n- Standards signoff: Allison Grant (SRE/observability), Marcus Lin (Security), Henry Cho (PM)\n\n## Next Review\n- Target: align this matrix to the final ADR text and conformance fixtures before stable releases.\n- Next scheduled review: 2026-02-28 (DevEx SDK sync)\n",

{
  "title": "SDK Parity Matrix: Auth, Retries, Timeouts, Streaming, and Error Taxonomy (Python / TypeScript / Go)",
  "space": "eng-developer-experience",
  "author": "Ibrahim Khan",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "in_review",
  "created_at": "2026-01-18",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-21",
  "reviewers": [
    "Monica Patel",
    "Dana Lo",
    "Mateusz Zielinski",
    "Sabrina James",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Henry Cho"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sdk-parity",
    "auth",
    "retries",
    "timeouts",
    "streaming",
    "error-taxonomy",
    "devex"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/sdk-parity-audit-overview.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json",
    "sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sdk-auth-resolution-and-secret-handling.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-retry-policy-v1.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-timeout-model.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "## Purpose
This page is the working parity matrix for the cross-language SDK parity initiative. It documents **current behavior** and **target behavior** across:
- **redwood-sdk-python**
- **redwood-sdk-typescript**
- **redwood-sdk-go**

The matrix is used as:
1) the source-of-truth for what “parity” means for auth/retry/timeout/streaming/error behavior,
2) the checklist for code changes and docs updates, and
3) the basis for the cross-language conformance test suite.

## Scope
In scope:
- API key / bearer token auth resolution order, env var naming, headers
- Retry policy: retryable status codes, network errors, backoff/jitter, respect Retry-After
- Timeout model: connect/read/overall semantics and defaults
- Streaming behavior: disconnects, partial output, cancellation, retry guidance
- Error taxonomy: typed errors + standardized fields (request_id, retry_count, timeout_ms, etc.)

Out of scope:
- New auth mechanisms (e.g., OAuth flows)
- Major API surface redesign
- Streaming “exactly once” semantics (SDKs remain conservative; idempotency guidance is documented)

## Target Standard (summary)
This is the parity target (see linked standards/ADRs for the full rationale):

### Auth resolution order (all SDKs)
1. **Explicit client configuration** (e.g., constructor `api_key` / `token`)
2. **Environment variables** (preferred names)
3. Optional: shared config file is **not** supported in v1 parity scope

Preferred env vars:
- `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (primary)
- `REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN` (if using bearer tokens)
- `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` (optional; defaults to hosted API)

Header rules:
- API key: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (consistent across SDKs)
- Never log secrets; error messages must be redaction-safe

### Retry policy defaults (all SDKs)
- Max attempts: **4 total** (1 initial + up to 3 retries)
- Retryable HTTP status codes:
  - **429** (rate limited) — must respect `Retry-After`
  - **408** (request timeout)
  - **409** (conflict) only when `code` indicates transient (see error taxonomy below)
  - **5xx** (500, 502, 503, 504)
- Retryable network errors:
  - DNS errors, connection refused/reset, TLS handshake errors, socket timeouts, unexpected EOF
- Non-retryable:
  - **4xx** by default (400, 401, 403, 404, 422) unless explicitly documented and flagged retryable by server error `code`
- Backoff:
  - Exponential backoff with jitter
  - Base delay: **250ms**
  - Max delay: **8s**
  - Jitter: full jitter (random in [0, delay])
- Retry-After:
  - Parse `Retry-After` as either seconds or HTTP date
  - When present and valid, it overrides backoff for the next sleep (bounded by a max of 60s)

### Timeout model defaults (all SDKs)
Timeouts are expressed as **overall** plus optional granular timeouts.
- Default connect timeout: **10s**
- Default read timeout (non-streaming): **60s**
- Default overall timeout (non-streaming): **90s**
- Streaming:
  - Overall timeout applies to request setup (connect + first byte)
  - Streaming read is governed by an **idle timeout** (no bytes received) default **30s** (configurable)
  - Streaming must support user cancellation (AbortController/context/cancel token) and must terminate promptly

### Streaming retry guidance (all SDKs)
- **No automatic retry after partial streaming output** (to avoid duplicate side effects / duplicated tokens)
- If the connection fails **before first content event**, SDK may retry (subject to retry policy) when safe
- If failure happens **after partial output**, SDK raises a typed streaming interruption error containing:
  - request_id (if known)
  - bytes/events received count (best effort)
  - partial text (if buffering is enabled) or the last event seen
- Docs recommend:
  - use request_id for support
  - use idempotency keys for non-streaming or “safe-to-retry” flows

### Error taxonomy + fields (all SDKs)
All SDKs should expose typed errors with consistent fields:
- `message` (string; redaction-safe)
- `request_id` (string; from response headers/body when available)
- `status_code` (int; if HTTP response exists)
- `code` (string; Redwood error code enum)
- `retryable` (bool)
- `retry_after_ms` (int; when available)
- `attempt` / `retries` (int; how many retries already performed)
- `timeout_ms` (int; the configured timeout that triggered the failure, when applicable)
- `cause` / `wrapped_error` (language-native error, if exposed)


---

## Parity Matrix
Legend:
- ✅ = matches target
- ⚠️ = partially matches / edge cases
- ❌ = mismatch

### A) Authentication
| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Env var names recognized | ⚠️ `REDWOOD_API_KEY` plus legacy `RW_API_KEY` in some examples | ⚠️ `REDWOOD_API_KEY` + `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in older versions | ⚠️ `REDWOOD_API_KEY` + `REDWOOD_BEARER` in older builds | `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN`, `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` only (legacy allowed with deprecation warnings) | Align naming; add migration messaging | Sabrina / Dana / Mateusz |
| Resolution order | ⚠️ explicit param wins; env fallback; but error text differs by path | ✅ explicit param wins; env fallback | ⚠️ env sometimes overrides when both set due to init helper | Explicit > env > error | Fix Go init helper precedence; standardize error text | Mateusz |
| Header format | ✅ `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | ⚠️ some endpoints set `X-Api-Key` in older compatibility layer | ✅ Bearer | Bearer everywhere | TS must stop emitting `X-Api-Key` unless explicitly configured (compat) | Dana |
| Missing auth error | ⚠️ raises generic ValueError with setup message | ⚠️ throws Error without remediation guidance | ⚠️ returns error without indicating env var names | Typed AuthError with message listing supported env vars (no secret echo) | Standardize message template | Ibrahim |
| Secret redaction in logs | ⚠️ redacts in most paths, but debug mode can leak headers in Python | ✅ redacts | ⚠️ Go debug logs included full headers in one helper | Never log `Authorization`; redact known token patterns | Security signoff required; add tests | Marcus + language owners |


### B) Retry Policy / Backoff / Retry-After
| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default max attempts | ⚠️ 3 total in some clients; 4 in others | ✅ 4 total | ⚠️ 5 total (historical) | 4 total | Align defaults + docs | Ibrahim |
| Retryable status codes | ⚠️ retries 429 + 5xx; 408 inconsistent | ⚠️ one bug: retried 400 in middleware edge case | ⚠️ retries 429 + 5xx but missed 408 | Retry 429/408/5xx; 409 only when transient | Fix TS 400 retry; include 408 across all | Dana / Sabrina / Mateusz |
| Network error retries | ✅ connection errors retried | ⚠️ fetch abort handling categorized incorrectly | ✅ net/http errors retried | Retry network errors; do not retry user cancellations | TS must differentiate AbortController cancel vs network failure | Dana |
| Backoff + jitter | ⚠️ exponential but jitter differs; base delay not consistent | ⚠️ jitter added but not full-jitter | ✅ close to target | Base 250ms; max 8s; full jitter | Normalize algorithms; align test fixtures | Ibrahim |
| Retry-After parsing | ✅ parses seconds; date format missing | ✅ parses seconds + date | ❌ ignores Retry-After | Parse seconds/date; override backoff; max 60s | Go must implement; Python add date parsing | Mateusz / Sabrina |
| Retry instrumentation fields | ⚠️ logs attempt count but not standardized keys | ⚠️ request_id missing on some retry errors | ❌ no consistent fields | Standard fields: request_id, retry_count, retry_reason, retry_after_ms | Align logging schema; docs | Logan Wright + Nadia Rahman |


### C) Timeouts
| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Timeout configuration surface | ⚠️ `timeout` overloaded; connect/read not consistently exposed | ⚠️ per-request abort only; defaults not obvious | ✅ context + client timeout exists, but mapping inconsistent | Provide overall + connect/read/idle (stream) where supported; map consistently | Align naming + docs snippets across languages | Ibrahim + language owners |
| Default connect timeout | ⚠️ 5s in one client | ✅ 10s | ⚠️ OS default (unbounded) when context missing | 10s | Ensure Go always sets connect timeout when using default client | Mateusz |
| Default overall timeout (non-stream) | ⚠️ 60s | ✅ 90s | ⚠️ 120s | 90s | Normalize; include migration notes | Henry + DevEx |
| Streaming timeout semantics | ❌ streaming ignored `timeout` in iterator path (support driver SUP-29410) | ⚠️ abort cancels fetch, but idle timeout not implemented | ⚠️ context cancel works, but idle timeout not consistent | Streaming: connect/first-byte uses overall; read idle timeout default 30s | Implement idle timeout for TS/Go; fix Python honoring timeouts in stream | Sabrina / Dana / Mateusz |
| User cancellation | ✅ `KeyboardInterrupt`/cancel bubbles; explicit cancel supported | ✅ AbortController supported | ✅ context cancellation supported | All must stop promptly and surface as CancelledError (not retryable) | Ensure cancellation is never retried; consistent error type | Ibrahim |


### D) Streaming Semantics / Edge Cases
| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Event model | ⚠️ yields raw chunks in some examples; structured events elsewhere | ✅ structured events (`message.delta`, `message.completed`, etc.) | ⚠️ mixed: some helpers emit raw lines | Standardize event names + payload fields in docs; keep language-idiomatic wrappers | Docs + examples must match; conformance fixtures for event ordering | Wei Chen + language owners |
| Partial output on disconnect | ⚠️ partial text lost if exception thrown mid-chunk | ✅ surfaces partial text in most cases | ⚠️ surfaces last event only | Typed StreamingInterruptedError includes partial output when available | Decide buffering policy (memory tradeoff) and document it | Ibrahim + Henry |
| Disconnect classification | ⚠️ raised as generic connection error | ⚠️ sometimes treated as retryable network error even after content | ⚠️ ambiguous EOF vs server close | If disconnect after content: not auto-retry; raise streaming interruption (retryable=false) | Fix classification and retry suppression | Dana / Mateusz |
| Retry behavior for streaming | ⚠️ may retry pre-first-event; inconsistent | ⚠️ retried after some events in one path | ✅ generally no retry after events | Only retry if no content delivered yet; never after partial | Conformance test should simulate “first token then FIN” | Ibrahim |
| Proxy buffering / keep-alives | ⚠️ no documented guidance | ⚠️ no documented guidance | ⚠️ some guidance in README only | Document recommended keep-alive/idle timeout settings and proxy caveats | Capture in streaming guide + quickstarts | Wei Chen |


### E) Error Taxonomy (Typed Errors + Fields)
| Behavior | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Target (desired) | Gap / Notes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base error type | ⚠️ multiple base classes across modules | ⚠️ Error subclasses exist but missing consistent fields | ⚠️ errors wrap net/http without stable fields | Single family: RedwoodError + typed subclasses | Align naming; publish mapping table | Ibrahim |
| request_id propagation | ⚠️ missing on some streaming exceptions | ✅ present for most HTTP errors | ❌ missing in some cases | request_id always present when server emitted it; best effort on network failures | Requires gateway + SDK work; ensure header parsing in all clients | Ethan Park + language owners |
| retryable flag | ⚠️ computed ad-hoc | ⚠️ present but not always accurate | ❌ absent | Always compute using standard classifier; included on error | Shared classifier behavior via fixtures | Ibrahim |
| Error `code` field | ⚠️ present only when JSON body parses | ✅ present | ⚠️ present but naming differs | Use Redwood error code enum; consistent string values | Ensure OpenAI-compat surfaces same fields | Ibrahim |
| Safe error messages (no secrets) | ⚠️ some include base URL with query params | ✅ safe | ✅ safe | No tokens/headers; sanitize URLs; include remediation | Add lint/tests for common secret patterns | Marcus Lin |


---

## Open Questions / Decisions Needed
1) **Legacy env vars support window**: Do we allow `RW_API_KEY` / `REDWOOD_TOKEN` / `REDWOOD_BEARER` for one minor release with deprecation warnings, or do we drop immediately?
   - Proposed: support for **2 minor releases**, with warnings and migration guide.

2) **Streaming buffering policy** for partial output: Should SDKs buffer full generated text by default to include it in StreamingInterruptedError?
   - Proposed: default **no full buffering** (stream-first), but include:
     - `last_event` (always)
     - optional `partial_text` when the SDK already has it (e.g., user concatenates deltas)
     - optional `buffer_output=true` option (document memory risk)

3) **409 retry semantics**: Which error codes should be considered transient (retryable) under 409?
   - Proposed: retry 409 only when server error `code` in allowlist (to be defined in error code enum docs).

4) **Timeout defaults for enterprise**: Some customers want stricter defaults (e.g., overall 30s). Do we provide a named preset (e.g., `timeouts="interactive"`) or keep only numeric config?
   - Proposed: numeric config only for v1 parity; presets can be introduced later.

5) **Telemetry/analytics**: For environments where telemetry is not permitted, do we require standardized structured logs only?
   - Proposed: minimum requirement is standardized logger/hook fields; telemetry remains opt-in per SDK policy.


## Acceptance Criteria (Parity Definition)
Parity is “done” when all conditions below are met:

### Functional parity
- Auth:
  - Explicit credentials always override env vars
  - Env var names and missing-auth errors are consistent (including remediation text)
  - Secrets are never logged in any mode
- Retries:
  - Same retryable status codes and network errors
  - Same defaults: max_attempts=4, base=250ms, max=8s, full jitter
  - All SDKs respect Retry-After (seconds + HTTP date)
  - Cancellation is never retried
- Timeouts:
  - Defaults match (connect=10s, read=60s, overall=90s)
  - Streaming honors connect/first-byte timeouts and idle timeout (30s default)
- Streaming:
  - No automatic retries after partial output
  - Typed streaming interruption errors contain request_id when available and a stable reason
- Errors:
  - Typed errors across SDKs expose: message, request_id, status_code, code, retryable, retry_after_ms, attempt/retries

### Test and docs parity
- Conformance suite passes for all SDKs:
  - 429 + Retry-After seconds
  - 429 + Retry-After HTTP date
  - 5xx retry with jitter bounds
  - network reset mid-request
  - streaming disconnect before first event (may retry)
  - streaming disconnect after N events (must not auto-retry)
- Docs pages and quickstarts show the same option names and recommended defaults across languages.

### Operational readiness
- Standardized log/hook fields available:
  - `request_id`, `retry_count`, `retry_reason`, `retry_after_ms`, `timeout_ms`, `streaming_disconnect_reason`
- Rollout dashboard includes dimensions by SDK + version (where available).


## Notes on Top Support Drivers (why we’re doing this)
- Streaming timeouts not honored in Python streaming iterator path (repro’d; aligns with SUP-29410)
- TS retry bug retried non-retryable 400 in one middleware edge case (billing concern; SUP-29438)
- Go ignored Retry-After on 429 (burst retries; SUP-29477)
- Enterprise proxy environments cause streaming disconnects; need consistent error surfaces + guidance (SUP-29505)


## Change Tracking / How to Update This Matrix
- Each row should be updated when:
  - a parity PR merges, or
  - conformance tests uncover a mismatch
- When updating, include:
  - “current” column changes (what is now true)
  - “gap/notes” updates (what remains)
  - link to the PR/ticket in the appropriate repo (via the parity epic)

## Ownership
- DRI: Monica Patel
- Tech lead: Ibrahim Khan
- Language owners: Dana Lo (TS), Mateusz Zielinski (Go), Sabrina James (Python)
- Standards signoff: Allison Grant (SRE/observability), Marcus Lin (Security), Henry Cho (PM)

## Next Review
- Target: align this matrix to the final ADR text and conformance fixtures before stable releases.
- Next scheduled review: 2026-02-28 (DevEx SDK sync)

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) \\u2014 Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Dev Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-07-18\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-09-05\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Lauren Bishop\",\n    \"Vanessa Ortiz\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"dedicated\",\n    \"autoscaling\",\n    \"predictive-scaling\",\n    \"known-issues\",\n    \"support-playbook\",\n    \"rollout\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/autoscaling-bounds-customer-escalation-playbook.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-troubleshooting-runbook.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/autoscaling-bounds-observability-dashboard-spec.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-and-predictive-mode-release-notes.json\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"h1. Overview\\nPredictive autoscaling is an opt-in mode for *Redwood Dedicated* that biases scale decisions using forecasted demand (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events, historical request rates/latency). Predictive mode *does not* override customer-configured *min/max bounds* and will fall back to reactive signals when forecasts are stale/unavailable.\\n\\nThis page lists the most common *known issues* observed during pilot/canary, how to recognize them, and recommended *workarounds* for Customer Success and Support. This is not a full runbook; for deep debugging and mitigations, use the dedicated on-call runbook linked above.\\n\\nh2. Scope / When this page applies\\n* Applies to:* Dedicated deployments with predictive mode enabled (feature-flagged per account/deployment).\\n* Not applicable to:* Hosted API autoscaling or Dedicated deployments running reactive-only scaling.\\n\\nh2. Quick definitions (customer-friendly)\\n* *Forecast / prediction:* A projected target capacity (replicas/GPU slices) for an upcoming time window.\\n* *Reactive scaling:* Signals like queue depth, saturation, and latency that trigger scaling based on current conditions.\\n* *Bounds:* Customer-configured *min* and *max* capacity. The autoscaler clamps desired capacity within these bounds.\\n* *Bound-hit:* When the autoscaler wants to go above max or below min but is prevented by bounds.\\n\\nh1. Rollout caveats (read first)\\n1) *Opt-in + guarded rollout:* Predictive mode is still rolling out. Some regions/accounts may not be eligible.\\n2) *Model/workload sensitivity:* Highly bursty workloads with low steady-state traffic can produce noisy forecasts.\\n3) *Do not promise \\u201cno queueing\\u201d under max bounds:* If traffic exceeds max-bound capacity and the region cannot burst, queueing/latency can occur. This is expected behavior; the product surfaces it via bound-hit metrics.\\n4) *Time-to-effect:* Changes to predictive settings may take up to *10\\u201320 minutes* to reflect in decisions (depending on caching and evaluation intervals).\\n\\nh1. Known issues & workarounds\\n\\nh2. 1) False positives (over-scaling before traffic arrives)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Capacity ramps up early; customer sees increased spend/idle utilization.\\n* Forecast line is above actual demand; prediction error is consistently positive.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Holidays/product changes make recent history unrepresentative.\\n* Scheduled-event definitions are too broad (e.g., daily job marked as \\u201chigh\\u201d when it is moderate).\\n* Low-volume workloads where small absolute errors become large relative errors.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) *Reduce predictive bias* (preferred): switch to \\u201cPredictive + Reactive Override\\u201d (if available in the customer\\u2019s build) or lower the predictive weight via internal config (eng-assisted).\\n2) *Use a tighter max bound* to cap spend if the customer\\u2019s primary concern is budget.\\n3) If customer can tolerate brief queueing, recommend *reactive-only* during the window and re-enable predictive after retraining/after a week of stable traffic.\\n\\n*Support notes*\\n* Collect: deployment_id, region, last 7 days of request rate, and a screenshot of desired vs bounded capacity.\\n* If the customer is in contract negotiation over cost ceilings, steer toward bounds and recommended ranges, not predictive promises.\\n\\nh2. 2) Timezone misalignment (forecast ramps at the wrong local time)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Customer reports \\u201cit scales for our ramp, but 1\\u20133 hours too early/late.\\u201d\\n* Recurring daily ramp shows a consistent offset.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Traffic exhibits local-time patterns but the forecast is effectively aligned to UTC (or mis-tagged timezone).\\n* Scheduled events were provided in local time but entered/processed as UTC.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Confirm the customer\\u2019s *operational timezone* and the timezone assumed for any scheduled events.\\n2) Temporary mitigation: set a *higher min bound* covering the ramp window until timezone is corrected.\\n3) If the account uses scheduled events: update the event schedule with explicit timezone (eng-assisted if the UI/API does not expose timezone selection yet).\\n\\n*Escalation trigger*\\n* If offset is consistent and reproducible, file an escalation to Eng Infra with: account_id, deployment_id, region, customer timezone, and at least two days of graphs showing the offset.\\n\\nh2. 3) Insufficient history (under-scaling because the predictor lacks training data)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Predictive mode enabled, but scaling behaves similar to reactive-only.\\n* Forecast confidence is low or \\u201cnot available\\u201d; autoscaler logs indicate fallback to reactive.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* New deployment or new model route without enough steady history.\\n* Major traffic shape change in the last few days.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Set a *conservative min bound* aligned to baseline throughput to avoid cold starts.\\n2) Use *reactive-only* for the first 1\\u20132 weeks of a new deployment, then re-enable predictive mode once traffic stabilizes.\\n3) If ramp is known and contractual, use *scheduled events* (if enabled for the account) as an interim signal source.\\n\\n*Support note*\\n* \\u201cPredictive mode\\u201d is not a guarantee; it is a best-effort bias that requires stable patterns.\\n\\nh2. 4) Stale forecast / prediction pipeline outage (sudden behavior change)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Predictive scaling appears to stop; capacity only changes after queue depth increases.\\n* UI shows forecast timestamp is old, or \\u201cforecast unavailable.\\u201d\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Forecast provider returned stale data; the autoscaler rejected it due to staleness checks.\\n* Regional data pipeline delay.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Treat as expected fail-safe: *reactive scaling takes over*.\\n2) Raise min bound temporarily for the affected ramp window.\\n3) If customer is impacted (p95 latency regression), advise disabling predictive mode until pipeline recovers.\\n\\n*Escalation trigger*\\n* Any incident where stale forecasts correlate with user-visible latency/SLO breach: escalate to SRE per the Dedicated autoscaler runbook.\\n\\nh2. 5) Oscillation / capacity jitter (scale up/down thrash)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Replicas/GPU count changes frequently (e.g., every few minutes).\\n* Customer sees request latency jitter; autoscaler event stream shows alternating scale-up and scale-down.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Noisy predictions combined with aggressive cooldowns.\\n* Workload has spiky batch traffic that looks like repeated ramps.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Increase *cooldown* / dampening parameters (eng-assisted if not customer-configurable yet).\\n2) Increase *min step size* for scale changes (avoid micro-adjustments).\\n3) Prefer reactive signals for scale-down, predictive for scale-up (hybrid mode) where available.\\n4) If the customer is latency-sensitive, disable predictive temporarily and stabilize with min bound.\\n\\n*Support note*\\n* If a pilot customer reports oscillation, check whether they are on the build containing anti-oscillation guardrails. If not, coordinate an upgrade or disable predictive.\\n\\nh2. 6) Null/empty prediction edge case (unsafe downscale risk)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* A forecast response contains null/empty values; desired capacity appears to drop unexpectedly.\\n\\n*Status*\\n* Mitigated by a hotfix to prevent scale-to-zero when predictor returns null. Some older pilot environments may not have the fix.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) If suspected: disable predictive mode immediately and set min bound to a safe baseline.\\n2) Escalate to Eng Infra with urgency and include timestamps + deployment_id.\\n\\nh2. 7) Max-bound saturation (predictive wants more capacity than allowed)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Queue depth increases during ramp; customer sees \\u201cwe told it to scale, but it didn\\u2019t.\\u201d\\n* Metrics show frequent *max-bound hit* events.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* The customer\\u2019s max bound is below what the workload requires for the ramp.\\n* Region capacity shortage prevents provisioning even below max (rare but possible).\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Clarify intent: if max bound is a *hard budget cap*, then queueing is an expected tradeoff.\\n2) If customer goal is SLA/latency, recommend increasing max bound or using burst capacity (if contract allows).\\n3) For predictable ramps: raise min bound ahead of the ramp so the system is already warm.\\n\\n*Escalation trigger*\\n* If min bound cannot be met due to region shortage, treat as a reliability event (see shortage behavior in the runbook).\\n\\nh1. What to ask the customer (minimum checklist)\\n1) Deployment name / deployment_id and region\\n2) Current bounds: min, max, cooldowns (if known)\\n3) Predictive mode state (enabled? hybrid? scheduled events?)\\n4) The customer\\u2019s local timezone and the time window of the ramp\\n5) Impact statement: spend concern vs latency/SLA concern\\n6) Screenshots or exports of: desired vs bounded capacity, queue depth, and p95 latency over the affected window\\n\\nh1. Recommended customer guidance (safe, non-committal language)\\n* \\u201cPredictive autoscaling helps pre-warm capacity for repeating traffic patterns, but it still respects your min/max bounds and will fall back to reactive scaling when forecasts are not available.\\u201d\\n* \\u201cIf the primary goal is controlling spend, set a max bound you\\u2019re comfortable with and we can tune predictive behavior to avoid early ramp-ups.\\u201d\\n* \\u201cIf the primary goal is meeting latency SLO during a known ramp, a higher baseline min (or scheduled event) is often the most reliable first step.\\u201d\\n\\nh1. When to escalate (internal)\\nEscalate to *Eng Infra / SRE* if any of the following are true:\\n* Predictive mode enabled and customer reports sustained latency regression (p95/p99) during a known ramp\\n* Reproducible timezone offset or consistently stale forecasts\\n* Oscillation causing user-visible impact\\n* Suspected null/empty prediction edge case\\n* Min bound cannot be met (possible region shortage)\\n\\nInclude in escalation: account_id, deployment_id, region, timestamps, graphs for queue depth + desired/bounded capacity, and whether disabling predictive mitigates.\\n\\nh1. Changelog\\n* 2025-09-05: Updated mitigations for oscillation and clarified max-bound saturation guidance.\\n* 2025-08-02: Added null/empty prediction edge case and mitigation instructions.\\n* 2025-07-18: Initial publication for pilot support readiness.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_07daff0e8966460f86c297b6939b607a\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/predictive-autoscaling-known-issues.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\nconfidentiality : internal body : h1. overview predictive autoscaling is an opt - in mode for * redwood dedicated * that biases scale decisions using forecasted demand ( time - of - day patterns, scheduled events, historical request rates / latency ). predictive mode * does not * override customer - configured * min / max bounds * and will fall back to reactive signals when forecasts are stale / unavailable. this page lists the most common * known issues * observed during pilot / canary, how to recognize them, and recommended * workarounds * for customer success and support. this is not a full runbook ; for deep debugging and mitigations, use the dedicated on - call runbook linked above.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/predictive-autoscaling-known-issues.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\n- only. * forecast confidence is low or “ not available ” ; autoscaler logs indicate fallback to reactive. * likely causes * * new deployment or new model route without enough steady history. * major traffic shape change in the last few days. * recommended workarounds * 1 ) set a * conservative min bound * aligned to baseline throughput to avoid cold starts. 2 ) use * reactive - only * for the first 1 – 2 weeks of a new deployment, then re - enable predictive mode once traffic stabilizes. 3 ) if ramp is known and contractual, use * scheduled events * ( if enabled for the account ) as an interim signal source.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/predictive-autoscaling-known-issues.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\n##hots or exports of : desired vs bounded capacity, queue depth, and p95 latency over the affected window h1. recommended customer guidance ( safe, non - committal language ) * “ predictive autoscaling helps pre - warm capacity for repeating traffic patterns, but it still respects your min / max bounds and will fall back to reactive scaling when forecasts are not available. ” * “ if the primary goal is controlling spend, set a max bound you ’ re comfortable with and we can tune predictive behavior to avoid early ramp - ups. ” * “ if the primary goal is meeting latency slo during a known ramp, a higher baseline min ( or scheduled event ) is often the most reliable first step. ”",

document.title: Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds
document.content:
{
  "title": "Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Dev Patel",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-07-18",
  "last_updated": "2025-09-05",
  "reviewers": [
    "Lauren Bishop",
    "Vanessa Ortiz",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Allison Grant"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "dedicated",
    "autoscaling",
    "predictive-scaling",
    "known-issues",
    "support-playbook",
    "rollout"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/autoscaling-bounds-customer-escalation-playbook.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-troubleshooting-runbook.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/autoscaling-bounds-observability-dashboard-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json",
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-and-predictive-mode-release-notes.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "h1. Overview
Predictive autoscaling is an opt-in mode for *Redwood Dedicated* that biases scale decisions using forecasted demand (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events, historical request rates/latency). Predictive mode *does not* override customer-configured *min/max bounds* and will fall back to reactive signals when forecasts are stale/unavailable.

This page lists the most common *known issues* observed during pilot/canary, how to recognize them, and recommended *workarounds* for Customer Success and Support. This is not a full runbook; for deep debugging and mitigations, use the dedicated on-call runbook linked above.

h2. Scope / When this page applies
* Applies to:* Dedicated deployments with predictive mode enabled (feature-flagged per account/deployment).
* Not applicable to:* Hosted API autoscaling or Dedicated deployments running reactive-only scaling.

h2. Quick definitions (customer-friendly)
* *Forecast / prediction:* A projected target capacity (replicas/GPU slices) for an upcoming time window.
* *Reactive scaling:* Signals like queue depth, saturation, and latency that trigger scaling based on current conditions.
* *Bounds:* Customer-configured *min* and *max* capacity. The autoscaler clamps desired capacity within these bounds.
* *Bound-hit:* When the autoscaler wants to go above max or below min but is prevented by bounds.

h1. Rollout caveats (read first)
1) *Opt-in + guarded rollout:* Predictive mode is still rolling out. Some regions/accounts may not be eligible.
2) *Model/workload sensitivity:* Highly bursty workloads with low steady-state traffic can produce noisy forecasts.
3) *Do not promise “no queueing” under max bounds:* If traffic exceeds max-bound capacity and the region cannot burst, queueing/latency can occur. This is expected behavior; the product surfaces it via bound-hit metrics.
4) *Time-to-effect:* Changes to predictive settings may take up to *10–20 minutes* to reflect in decisions (depending on caching and evaluation intervals).

h1. Known issues & workarounds

h2. 1) False positives (over-scaling before traffic arrives)
*Symptoms*
* Capacity ramps up early; customer sees increased spend/idle utilization.
* Forecast line is above actual demand; prediction error is consistently positive.

*Likely causes*
* Holidays/product changes make recent history unrepresentative.
* Scheduled-event definitions are too broad (e.g., daily job marked as “high” when it is moderate).
* Low-volume workloads where small absolute errors become large relative errors.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) *Reduce predictive bias* (preferred): switch to “Predictive + Reactive Override” (if available in the customer’s build) or lower the predictive weight via internal config (eng-assisted).
2) *Use a tighter max bound* to cap spend if the customer’s primary concern is budget.
3) If customer can tolerate brief queueing, recommend *reactive-only* during the window and re-enable predictive after retraining/after a week of stable traffic.

*Support notes*
* Collect: deployment_id, region, last 7 days of request rate, and a screenshot of desired vs bounded capacity.
* If the customer is in contract negotiation over cost ceilings, steer toward bounds and recommended ranges, not predictive promises.

h2. 2) Timezone misalignment (forecast ramps at the wrong local time)
*Symptoms*
* Customer reports “it scales for our ramp, but 1–3 hours too early/late.”
* Recurring daily ramp shows a consistent offset.

*Likely causes*
* Traffic exhibits local-time patterns but the forecast is effectively aligned to UTC (or mis-tagged timezone).
* Scheduled events were provided in local time but entered/processed as UTC.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Confirm the customer’s *operational timezone* and the timezone assumed for any scheduled events.
2) Temporary mitigation: set a *higher min bound* covering the ramp window until timezone is corrected.
3) If the account uses scheduled events: update the event schedule with explicit timezone (eng-assisted if the UI/API does not expose timezone selection yet).

*Escalation trigger*
* If offset is consistent and reproducible, file an escalation to Eng Infra with: account_id, deployment_id, region, customer timezone, and at least two days of graphs showing the offset.

h2. 3) Insufficient history (under-scaling because the predictor lacks training data)
*Symptoms*
* Predictive mode enabled, but scaling behaves similar to reactive-only.
* Forecast confidence is low or “not available”; autoscaler logs indicate fallback to reactive.

*Likely causes*
* New deployment or new model route without enough steady history.
* Major traffic shape change in the last few days.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Set a *conservative min bound* aligned to baseline throughput to avoid cold starts.
2) Use *reactive-only* for the first 1–2 weeks of a new deployment, then re-enable predictive mode once traffic stabilizes.
3) If ramp is known and contractual, use *scheduled events* (if enabled for the account) as an interim signal source.

*Support note*
* “Predictive mode” is not a guarantee; it is a best-effort bias that requires stable patterns.

h2. 4) Stale forecast / prediction pipeline outage (sudden behavior change)
*Symptoms*
* Predictive scaling appears to stop; capacity only changes after queue depth increases.
* UI shows forecast timestamp is old, or “forecast unavailable.”

*Likely causes*
* Forecast provider returned stale data; the autoscaler rejected it due to staleness checks.
* Regional data pipeline delay.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Treat as expected fail-safe: *reactive scaling takes over*.
2) Raise min bound temporarily for the affected ramp window.
3) If customer is impacted (p95 latency regression), advise disabling predictive mode until pipeline recovers.

*Escalation trigger*
* Any incident where stale forecasts correlate with user-visible latency/SLO breach: escalate to SRE per the Dedicated autoscaler runbook.

h2. 5) Oscillation / capacity jitter (scale up/down thrash)
*Symptoms*
* Replicas/GPU count changes frequently (e.g., every few minutes).
* Customer sees request latency jitter; autoscaler event stream shows alternating scale-up and scale-down.

*Likely causes*
* Noisy predictions combined with aggressive cooldowns.
* Workload has spiky batch traffic that looks like repeated ramps.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Increase *cooldown* / dampening parameters (eng-assisted if not customer-configurable yet).
2) Increase *min step size* for scale changes (avoid micro-adjustments).
3) Prefer reactive signals for scale-down, predictive for scale-up (hybrid mode) where available.
4) If the customer is latency-sensitive, disable predictive temporarily and stabilize with min bound.

*Support note*
* If a pilot customer reports oscillation, check whether they are on the build containing anti-oscillation guardrails. If not, coordinate an upgrade or disable predictive.

h2. 6) Null/empty prediction edge case (unsafe downscale risk)
*Symptoms*
* A forecast response contains null/empty values; desired capacity appears to drop unexpectedly.

*Status*
* Mitigated by a hotfix to prevent scale-to-zero when predictor returns null. Some older pilot environments may not have the fix.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) If suspected: disable predictive mode immediately and set min bound to a safe baseline.
2) Escalate to Eng Infra with urgency and include timestamps + deployment_id.

h2. 7) Max-bound saturation (predictive wants more capacity than allowed)
*Symptoms*
* Queue depth increases during ramp; customer sees “we told it to scale, but it didn’t.”
* Metrics show frequent *max-bound hit* events.

*Likely causes*
* The customer’s max bound is below what the workload requires for the ramp.
* Region capacity shortage prevents provisioning even below max (rare but possible).

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Clarify intent: if max bound is a *hard budget cap*, then queueing is an expected tradeoff.
2) If customer goal is SLA/latency, recommend increasing max bound or using burst capacity (if contract allows).
3) For predictable ramps: raise min bound ahead of the ramp so the system is already warm.

*Escalation trigger*
* If min bound cannot be met due to region shortage, treat as a reliability event (see shortage behavior in the runbook).

h1. What to ask the customer (minimum checklist)
1) Deployment name / deployment_id and region
2) Current bounds: min, max, cooldowns (if known)
3) Predictive mode state (enabled? hybrid? scheduled events?)
4) The customer’s local timezone and the time window of the ramp
5) Impact statement: spend concern vs latency/SLA concern
6) Screenshots or exports of: desired vs bounded capacity, queue depth, and p95 latency over the affected window

h1. Recommended customer guidance (safe, non-committal language)
* “Predictive autoscaling helps pre-warm capacity for repeating traffic patterns, but it still respects your min/max bounds and will fall back to reactive scaling when forecasts are not available.”
* “If the primary goal is controlling spend, set a max bound you’re comfortable with and we can tune predictive behavior to avoid early ramp-ups.”
* “If the primary goal is meeting latency SLO during a known ramp, a higher baseline min (or scheduled event) is often the most reliable first step.”

h1. When to escalate (internal)
Escalate to *Eng Infra / SRE* if any of the following are true:
* Predictive mode enabled and customer reports sustained latency regression (p95/p99) during a known ramp
* Reproducible timezone offset or consistently stale forecasts
* Oscillation causing user-visible impact
* Suspected null/empty prediction edge case
* Min bound cannot be met (possible region shortage)

Include in escalation: account_id, deployment_id, region, timestamps, graphs for queue depth + desired/bounded capacity, and whether disabling predictive mitigates.

h1. Changelog
* 2025-09-05: Updated mitigations for oscillation and clarified max-bound saturation guidance.
* 2025-08-02: Added null/empty prediction edge case and mitigation instructions.
* 2025-07-18: Initial publication for pilot support readiness.",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"42812\",\n  \"title\": \"scheduled scale profiles + fairness-aware fleet scaler\",\n  \"author\": \"Asha Patel\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-22\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-02-22\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/fleet-scheduler-fairness-scaler\",\n  \"description\": \"Motivation: customers with mixed workloads asked for predictable dedicated capacity behavior during known peak windows (daily batch jobs, nightly ingest, marketing campaigns) while preserving per-tenant fairness and soft throughput guarantees. This PR introduces a scheduler-based scale profile concept plus a fairness-aware scaler that reserves and enforces tenant headroom percentages during scheduled windows.\\n\\nWhat this change does (high level): adds a ScaleProfile CRD-like config for Dedicated (stored in control plane tenant config), implements time-based scale profiles in the fleet autoscaler, and augments the scheduler to compute and enforce tenant headroom fractions. The scaler now supports: 1) scheduled up/down adjustments (scale profiles), 2) tenant-level soft guarantees (headroom_pct) that allocate reserved burst capacity, and 3) fairness rebalancing to avoid long-term capacity starvation.\\n\\nKey behaviors and guarantees: - Scheduled profiles are applied with configurable pre-warm lead time (default 10m) to allow provisioning GPU pools before the window. - Headroom_pct is a soft-guarantee: the allocator attempts to preserve the specified percent of spare capacity per tenant but will yield if global capacity becomes constrained. - Fairness rebalancer runs every 60s and tries to minimize sustained deviation from baseline allocations; it is low-priority and will not preempt active requests.\\n\\nBackward compatibility and migration: existing Dedicated configs continue to work. New config fields have defaults that preserve current autoscaler behavior (headroom_pct=0, no scheduled profiles). Migration plan: control plane database migration adds the scale_profiles table and backfills empty value; the fleet-controller tolerates both old and new records for 48 hours post-deploy.\\n\\nTesting and telemetry: end-to-end integration tests added for scheduled windows, pre-warm behavior, and fairness under contention. New metrics: fleet_scale_profile_applied{profile,name}, tenant_headroom_utilization_pct, fairness_rebalance_actions_total. Dashboards updated: Dedicated -> Capacity -> Scheduled Profiles; an alert (SLO) for pre-warm misses added (dedicated.prewarm.miss > 0 for 5m).\\n\\nRollout plan: staged rollout: control plane first (feature flag), then fleet-controller + autoscaler; feature flag can be turned off to restore legacy behavior. We will enable for internal QA for 48h, then enable for a subset of enterprise tenants, and finally full rollout.\\n\\nChecklist:\\n- [x] Autoscaler algorithm implemented and unit-tested\\n- [x] Scheduler integration + pre-warm hook\\n- [x] API surface for tenant scale profiles + schema migration\\n- [x] End-to-end tests for scheduled up/down and fairness rebalancing\\n- [x] Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting\\n- [x] Migration and rollback plan documented\\n\\nRelated items: Linear ENG-7321, ENG-7389; RFC: /docs/rfcs/fleet-schedule-profiles.md\\n\\nNotes: there are a few known follow-ups tracked in ENG-7420 (deterministic allocation ordering) and ENG-7471 (adaptive pre-warm based on historical cold-starts).\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"a1f3e9b  Implemented ScaleProfile config and DB migration\",\n    \"d4b2c88  Fleet scaler: scheduled window handling + pre-warm logic\",\n    \"9f7a21c  Introduced tenant headroom accounting and fairness rebalancer\",\n    \"be3d110  Expose new metrics and update dashboards\",\n    \"5c8a44d  Add e2e tests and integration harness updates\",\n    \"c2f90e7  Docs: RFC link, API examples and migration notes\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"21\",\n  \"additions\": \"1387\",\n  \"deletions\": \"492\",\n  \"files_changed\": [\n    \"fleet/controller/scale_profile.go  (new) - core scheduler for applying profiles and pre-warm hooks\",\n    \"fleet/controller/allocator.go  - add headroom accounting hooks and fairness rebalance loop\",\n    \"controlplane/api/tenant_config.proto  - add ScaleProfile message and headroom_pct field\",\n    \"db/migrations/2026_02_15_add_scale_profiles.sql  (new) - migration to add scale_profiles table\",\n    \"telemetry/metrics_registry.go  - register tenant_headroom_utilization_pct, fairness_rebalance_actions_total\",\n    \"ui/dashboards/dedicated_profiles.json  - dashboard for scheduled profiles and pre-warm telemetry\",\n    \"integration/tests/scheduled_profile_test.go  - e2e test exercising pre-warm and scheduled scale-up\",\n    \"docs/rfcs/fleet-schedule-profiles.md  - design doc and API examples\",\n    \"api/client/dedicated.go  - client helpers to read/write scale profiles\",\n    \"helm/values.yaml  - feature flag toggle for scale_profiles (default: false)\",\n    \"Makefile and CI pipeline updates  - add e2e job guard for feature flagged runs\"\n  ],\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Marco Rivera\",\n    \"Lina Chen\",\n    \"Priya Gupta\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"dedicated\",\n    \"autoscaling\",\n    \"runtime\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"perf\",\n    \"feature\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-7321\",\n    \"ENG-7389\",\n    \"ENG-7420\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"unit: pass (go test ./... 112s)\",\n    \"integration: pass (e2e with feature flag enabled)\",\n    \"lint: pass (golangci-lint)\",\n    \"helm: pass\",\n    \"deploy-preview: pass (staged control plane)\"\n  ],\n  \"review_comments\": [\n    \"Marco Rivera (requested changes): The pre-warm lead time default of 10m seems conservative for small clusters; can we make it adaptive or expose cluster-level override?\",\n    \"Asha Patel (reply): Added cluster_override_ms config and plan to follow up with ENG-7471 for adaptive pre-warm based on historical cold-starts. Kept default 10m to be safe for customers we've seen miss capacity in tests.\",\n    \"Lina Chen (comment): DB migration looks sound but please ensure the migration is idempotent across control plane replicas.\",\n    \"Asha Patel (reply): Verified idempotency; migration uses IF NOT EXISTS and a lightweight backfill job with a lock. Added unit tests for migration run twice.\",\n    \"Priya Gupta (approved): Verified e2e test cases for fairness under contention. Metrics are meaningful and dashboards look good. Approving for merge after CI passes.\"\n  ],\n  \"merge_method\": \"squash\",\n  \"merge_commit_summary\": \"squash: add scheduled scale profiles and fairness-aware fleet scaler; metrics, migration, and e2e tests\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Added scheduled scale profiles for Dedicated fleets and a fairness-aware fleet autoscaler. Operators can define time-based scale profiles to pre-warm capacity and set tenant headroom_pct to preserve burst capacity for important tenants. Metrics and dashboards added for observability. Feature is behind a control-plane feature flag and will be opt-in during rollout.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"summary\": \"Adds scheduled scaling profiles and a fairness-enabled autoscaler to improve predictability for scheduled workload peaks while preventing long-term tenant starvation. Includes API, migration, metrics, tests, and rollout plan.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_comments\",\n    \"release_notes\",\n    \"summary\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_28d4ab23e7c74795ac809e8d9deef9ad\"\n}",
